source.claim_boundary: S5 promotion ratified (D-43 round 2 passed; maintainer PR review 2026-07-19), scored under the frozen 2026-07-17 estimand/interval/coverage contract on the unchanged machine-strict conditional-Beta interior DGP. Leading with the worst-in-arm result per the frozen S0 section 5.3 rule: shared_g1024_m04 profile alpha_intercept (fixef:sd_phylo(spp_id):(Intercept), the log-baseline latent-SD intercept of sd(spp_id, level = "phylogenetic") ~ x_tau, truth log(0.30)) covers 1119/1199=0.9333 (MCSE 0.0072; exact 95% CI 0.9176-0.9467) -- mildly anti-conservative, not nominal -- before the nominal results below. Both exact promotion arms (distinct_g1024_m04, shared_g1024_m04; N=1200 attempted replicates each; g=1024,m=4; profile method, 95% two-sided) pass the frozen S0 section 5 calibration gate for both fixed direct-SD regression coefficients: distinct_g1024_m04 alpha_intercept 1130/1200=0.9417 (CI 0.9269-0.9542) and alpha_x (the latent-SD slope, truth 0.25) 1132/1200=0.9433 (CI 0.9287-0.9557), profile_finite_rate=1.000, zero failures; shared_g1024_m04 alpha_intercept 1119/1199=0.9333 (CI 0.9176-0.9467) and alpha_x 1140/1199=0.9508 (CI 0.9370-0.9623), profile_finite_rate=0.99917 (1/1200 tmbprofile calls failed on both coefficients: replicate 407, seed 1989879593, extra_coverage seed source, fit_success=TRUE, pdHess=TRUE; per the pre-registered S0 section 5.1 exclusion policy, coverage is computed over the remaining 1199 finite profiles and the exclusion is disclosed, not silently dropped). Both Wald and profile intervals are computed side by side and neither is assumed superior a priori (S0 section 4); Wald coverage is observed to be closely similar to profile throughout (distinct wald: alpha_intercept 0.9425, alpha_x 0.9450; shared wald: alpha_intercept 0.9342, alpha_x 0.9525) -- an observation, not a profile-superiority claim. Per the S0 section 7 seed policy, replicates 1-400 of each 1200-replicate arm reuse the frozen point-fit-recovery seeds, so this coverage evidence and the prior point-fit-recovery evidence are correlated draws from the same DGP realisations, not two independent confirmations. The residual mild anti-conservatism, most visible on the shared arm, should be read against a low phylogenetic effective sample size at this design (mean_effective_n_proxy ~2.3 despite g=1024, driven by mean off-diagonal phylogenetic correlation ~0.46), not attributed to raw g. Tau is latent location SD, not family sigma or phi. This promotes inference_ready_with_caveats for exactly the two g=1024,m=4 promotion arms; the shared g=256,m=2 stress cell and the g in {256,512} context cells give the directional coverage-vs-g trend only and do not promote (S0 section 8), and the shared_g256_m02 HOLD (one warning, pdHess=0.9975) is reported descriptively only, never pooled into this or any promotion or gate, and is not repaired. Excluded (S0 section 9 fence, verbatim): q>1; family-sigma phylogeny; random/hierarchical RHS in sd(); labels/slopes; REML; missing routes; other families; a coverage-correcting estimator (this arc assesses calibration, it does not build a correction); neighbouring SDs/species counts; supported/nominal claims; the shared_g256_m02 HOLD; the stopped campaign 1c9bfd5f; PR #788.

source.claim_boundary: interval_feasible only for the named cell x direct q2 structured mu1/mu2 SD target x frozen low-rung estimator-specific fixture using an exact retained unclamped tmbprofile receipt. Coverage, calibration, and bias were not evaluated; this does not establish inference readiness, provider/family/q2-wide support, ML-vs-REML comparison, slopes, sigma, rho, other rungs, or public interval guidance. Animal/relmat ML pairs share numerical DGP realizations and are not independent provider evidence. This spatial sd(group) interval is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). The retained evidence does not test that condition: its data-generating process builds the latent field from the same fixed-range kernel the model assumes, so the range was correct by construction and range misspecification remains unexamined for this cell.

source.claim_boundary: Exact target sd:mu:mu1:spatial(1 | p | site). A profile-likelihood interval for the mu1-side intercept-level spatial random-intercept SD exists and is well-formed under ML on arc4_q6_spatial_mu1_fixture (labelled bivariate q6 block spatial(1 + x + z | p | site, coords = coords) in both mu1 and mu2; 8x9 = 72-site coordinate grid, 20 observations per site = 1440 obs; true mu1 intercept-level spatial SD 0.45, independent of 0.30/0.25 mu1 random-slope SDs (x/z) and 0.40/0.28/0.22 mu2 random-intercept/slope SDs the labelled two-slope q6 grammar requires). Five seeds (2026080301-2026080305) share ONE seed family across the local point-fit gate and this promotion campaign: estimates 0.430/0.398/0.479/0.404/0.429, relative error 0.044/0.116/0.064/0.102/0.048 (mean 0.075), every value <0.35; all five 95% profile intervals bracket the true 0.45 ([0.364,0.517], [0.334,0.481], [0.405,0.575], [0.340,0.487], [0.361,0.516]), convergence 0, pdHess TRUE, profile_boundary FALSE, conf_status "profile" throughout. mc-0123 is the mu1 sibling of mc-0124 (already interval_feasible, ev-mc-0124-b3-q6-mu2-interval): B3's own runner (tools/run-b2-q6-proof-profile-cohort.R, source sha a8d068e641105473b3f30723a92c909467a46fac) is unreachable from this tree, so this is an INDEPENDENT fixture for the same target family, not a replay of mc-0124's exact DGP; mc-0124's evidence is separate and is NOT inherited here. The Arc 0 candidate manifest cited tools/b2-q6-q12-admission-contracts.R:b2_q6q12_fixture as this cell's fixture, but that file does not exist anywhere in this tree -- a manifest defect, not evidence for this promotion. The profiled target is ONE component of a labelled six-component spatial block in which 15 correlation parameters are free with true value zero, alongside free sigma1, sigma2 and rho12. Realized finite-sample correlations among the six nominally independent latent fields reached max|cor| 0.336-0.727 across the gate seeds, at and above the |cor| ~0.457 level that has previously produced an alternate local optimum mid-profile-sweep elsewhere; the interval was feasible despite this, which is evidence of robustness for this target, NOT evidence that the design separates the components. Interval-existence claim only -- no coverage, calibration, sibling-target (mu2), whole-q6, provider-wide, REML, or public guidance claim. This spatial sd(group) interval is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). The retained evidence does not test that condition: its data-generating process builds the latent field from the same fixed-range kernel the model assumes, so the range was correct by construction and range misspecification remains unexamined for this cell.
source.next_gate: Coverage/calibration remain out of scope; a separate goal is required.

source.claim_boundary: Joint all-attempt 95% endpoint profile calibration for direct sd_spatial1, sd_spatial2, and latent rho_spatial passes at exact tested M (36 sites x 3) and H (36 x 8) baseline-ring configurations; M is the lowest tested jointly passing rung and L (12 x 3) failed. Fixed-kappa bivariate-Gaussian REML only; no mesh intervals, range, slopes, q4+, non-Gaussian, spatial sigma, derived observed correlations, geometry robustness, or supported-tier claim. This spatial sd(group) interval is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). The retained evidence does not test that condition: its data-generating process builds the latent field from the same fixed-range kernel the model assumes, so the range was correct by construction and range misspecification remains unexamined for this cell.

source.claim_boundary: Exact target sd:mu:mu1:(1 | p | id). A profile-likelihood interval for the mu1-side marginal random-intercept SD exists and is well-formed under REML on arc2_biv_musigma_fixture(n_id=60, n_each=8) (a labelled (1 | p | id) block correlating the mu1 and sigma1 random intercepts of a bivariate Gaussian fit; true sd_mu1=0.6, true sd_sigma1=0.4, true correlation=0.3, n_each=8 sitting ON the within-group-replication floor already validated for this block shape, R/drmTMB.R:2254-2257, known-limitations.md:245-249). Five seeds share ONE seed family across the point-fit recovery gate and the profile-feasibility campaign: sd_mu1 estimates 0.639/0.614/0.570/0.643/0.586, relative error 0.065/0.024/0.050/0.072/0.023 (worst case 0.072), every value <0.35; all five 95% profile intervals bracket the true 0.6 ([0.525,0.790], [0.505,0.759], [0.463,0.711], [0.532,0.791], [0.484,0.722]), convergence 0, pdHess TRUE, profile_boundary FALSE, conf_status "profile" throughout. The prior harness for this exact DGP, sim3() in scratchpad/reml_parity_gaps_3A_ladder.R, captured ONLY point estimates -- never standard errors, confidence intervals, convergence codes, or pdHess -- and was therefore structurally incapable of supporting an interval-feasibility claim; arc2_biv_musigma_fixture() replaces it with a committed fixture the profile-feasibility runner fits directly. The REML validator (drm_validate_reml_spec_biv) does NOT reject this spec: a gate branch on spec$random$mu_sigma$n_cors was added by commit 99138cfa7 (2026-07-08 04:57) and REMOVED 34 minutes later by commit 1b3e852bb (2026-07-08 05:31), which documents the admission inline at R/drmTMB.R:2359-2363; verified empirically here too, since all five current-source fits on the unpatched (post-1b3e852bb) package converge without error. mc-0206 (sd_sigma1) is the matched scale-side sibling of the SAME labelled block and is separately evidenced. Interval-existence claim only -- no coverage, calibration, sibling-target, or public guidance claim.

source.claim_boundary: Pure-mu univariate Gaussian exact REML with constant residual scale `sigma ~ 1` and no sigma random effect. Admits only unlabelled `relmat(1 | group)` or an independent intercept plus one numeric slope `relmat(1 + x | group)`. The Totoro campaign used the `K` representation, `n_each=20`, and exactly `M={8,16,32}`: 2,400 paired recovery datasets (4,800 ML/REML fits) and 6,000 REML coverage fits (9,000 target profiles); every fit converged, every profile was valid/two-sided/finite, and target coverage was 0.932-0.960 (maximum MCSE 0.00796). `K`/`Q` parity is established only by deterministic fixtures, not by the multi-seed campaign. The fitted structured SD scale `s_j` gives covariance `s_j^2 K_h`; node `i` has marginal SD `s_j sqrt(K_h[ii])`, which equals `s_j` only when that diagonal entry is one. Coverage is inference-ready with caveats, not nominal. Labelled, slope-only, multiple-slope, matched `mu+sigma`, sigma-random-effect, bivariate, non-Gaussian, untested matrices or M, fixed-effect-profile, and `supported` claims remain excluded.

Coverage, calibration, and bias were not evaluated; this does not establish inference readiness, provider/family/q1-wide support, slopes, sigma, q2plus, labels, REML, other rungs, or public interval guidance. The NB2 animal/relmat pair share one numerical configuration and are not independent corroboration. This spatial sd(group) interval is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). The retained evidence does not test that condition: its data-generating process builds the latent field from the same fixed-range kernel the model assumes, so the range was correct by construction and range misspecification remains unexamined for this cell.

source.claim_boundary: interval_feasible only for this named cell x direct structured-q1 target x frozen low-rung source fixture with an exact retained unclamped tmbprofile receipt and the retained dense-LSS K=12 non-covering control. REML, Coverage, calibration, bias, replication, and inference readiness were not evaluated; this is not provider-, family-, q1-, or portfolio-wide support. This spatial sd(group) interval is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). The retained evidence does not test that condition: its data-generating process builds the latent field from the same fixed-range kernel the model assumes, so the range was correct by construction and range misspecification remains unexamined for this cell.

source.claim_boundary: DEMOTED 2026-08-15: diagnostic evidence only. The retained tmbprofile receipt is complete and well-formed, but the fixture generates the latent field from a different covariance than the fitted exp(-d/range) kernel, so the declared truth is not the model's estimand. Under the shape-vs-location contract adopted the same day (docs/design/255), the operative ground for sitting BELOW interval_feasible is that the same misspecification means the POINT estimate was never validly tested against a known truth either, so neither the interval-shape claim's point-report premise nor any location claim is earned; location_checked=failed records the bracketing miss separately. Original boundary, retained for scope detail: "interval_feasible only for mc-0494 x its two exact direct Student spatial mu SD targets x the frozen n32 x 20 high-information fixture, each with a retained complete unclamped tmbprofile receipt. This establishes neither whole-formula, other target, provider-wide, family-wide, coverage, calibration, inference-ready, public, nor API support. This spatial sd(group) interval is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). That condition is not met here: the retained fixture generates the latent field from a different covariance than the fitted kernel, and the 2026-08-15 interval-truth re-check found the retained interval does not contain the fixture's declared true value. This claim is not currently supported; it awaits a fixture repair and a re-run, and nothing here shows the route does not fit."

source.claim_boundary: Only unlabelled intercept-only spatial(1|site,coords=coords) mu field is admitted when a zi formula is present; sigma must stay fixed-effect-only and mu must carry no ordinary RE terms. Board row: fit_status=point_fit, interval_status=unsupported, coverage_status=unsupported, denominator_policy=no_denominator_local_debug_only -- a single local deterministic smoke fit, not a retained-denominator recovery study. Tests confirm convergence, pdHess, sdpars$mu, ranef("spatial_mu"), and a direct profile_targets() row, but this is not interval, coverage, inference_ready, or supported evidence. The spatial sd(group) estimate here is conditional on the correlation range: spatial(1 | group, coords = coords) fixes the exponential range at the median positive pairwise distance among those coords, falling back to the maximum when that median is not positive and finite, and never estimates it (R/drmTMB.R:13403-13407); a true correlation length away from that fixed value is absorbed by the estimated sd(group). This cell makes no interval claim, so the conditioning applies to its point-scale evidence.

source.claim_boundary: Exact target sd:sigma:phylo_interaction(1 | plant:pollinator). A profile-likelihood interval exists and is well-formed under ML for zi_nbinom2 sigma phylo_interaction q1 (true SD 0.60). Five-seed Totoro 135-trace campaign (tools/run-135-trace-campaign.R; source SHA 6618e4b30303f7815b272f709ac2c8d09089132d): estimates 0.557/0.524/0.675/0.638/0.550, all five 95% profile intervals bracket the true 0.60 ([0.411,0.756], [0.367,0.730], [0.497,0.917], [0.474,0.858], [0.398,0.752]), convergence 0, pdHess TRUE, profile_boundary FALSE, conf_status "profile", clamp_limited FALSE (computed), both-sides LR crossing and unimodality TRUE throughout. Targetwise interval feasibility only - five seeds, single stats::profile() call per seed (TMB::tmbprofile / grid engine). No coverage, calibration, or Type-I error claim follows. Five seeds establish that a profile interval is obtainable and locates the truth, not that its nominal level is correct. Documented ML sigma-axis low bias at small/moderate group counts; interval bracketing is therefore asymmetrically at risk on the upper endpoint. REML is unavailable for this family (drm_validate_reml_spec admits only Gaussian and binomial).

This is not a continuous missing predictor, not k>=2, not impute_joint, not FIML across a SEM, and not zi-*. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. Existing student missing-response cell is unchanged.
source.next_gate: G4/G5 interval and replicated coverage are outside this first student-response cell. Next #962 family is zi_poisson (wait on zi+mi composition).

source.claim_boundary: G3 point-fit recovery for a zi_poisson response with one binary mi() predictor in mu only and zi ~ 1 (drmTMB #962 / S6 A7 / D-23). tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-zi-poisson-response.R recovers mu c(0.4, 0.5, 0.7), zi intercept logit(pi)=-0.8, and mi_x c(0.3, 0.8) under MCAR (tolerance 0.15, seed 13) and under outcome-dependent MAR (tolerance 0.20, seed 21). A G2 manual ZIP-mixture 2-point-sum logLik identity matches the TMB objective (tolerance 1e-6). A null DGP with beta_x=0 still recovers beta_x~0 so extra zeros do not load onto x. This is not a continuous missing predictor, not k>=2, not impute_joint, not FIML across a SEM, not mi() on zi, and not zi_nbinom2. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. The 2-point sum inlines the ZIP mixture; it does not call the Poisson leaf.
source.next_gate: G4/G5 interval and replicated coverage are outside this first ZIP-response cell. Next leftover is zi_nbinom2 (extra sigma).
